title: Transfer sterile forceps from their peel pouch onto a sterile drape without contaminating the forceps or the drape
instruction: Transfer the sterile forceps from their peel pouch onto the green drape without contaminating them: only the forceps, the inside of the pouch and the drape are sterile, so the forceps may touch nothing else, and nothing but the forceps may touch the drape or the tray. Then put both pouch sheets in the waste bins and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Circulating nurses and surgical technologists open sterile instruments onto the sterile field many times a day, and nothing non-sterile may touch the instrument or the field on the way. The pouch's two sheets only part when they are pulled apart against each other: pulling one sheet alone drags the whole light pouch along.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A clear acrylic pouch holder on the centre line, from 5 to 25 cm forward: a base 20 by 6 cm with a slot 2.4 cm wide and 2.2 cm deep running front to back. (2) Standing in it, a sterile peel pouch, 16 cm long front to back (its middle 15 cm forward) and 6 cm tall up to its seal: a white medical-grade paper sheet on the left and a clear PET/PE film sheet on the right (printed with blue seal lines), 1 cm apart, sealed together along the front, back and bottom edges; each sheet weighs 12 g. Above the seal each sheet's top flap is folded outward, 12 cm out to its side and 3 cm wide, ending in a stiff card pull tab 2 cm long, 3.5 cm tall and 6 mm thick: blue on the paper's flap, 11.6 cm left of the centre line, orange on the film's, 11.6 cm right of it, both 15 cm forward with their tops 8.8 cm above the table. The seal holds the sheets together until they are pulled 12 mm apart (about 7 N), then lets go. (3) Inside the pouch, lying front to back on the bottom seal, stainless-steel dressing forceps 12.4 cm long (30 g). (4) A stainless-steel instrument tray lined with a green cotton drape (the sterile field), inside 18 by 30 cm (from 27 to 45 cm forward, from 15 cm right to 15 cm left of the centre line), with a 1.5 cm rim. (5) Two grey polypropylene waste bins, inside 20 by 16 cm and 3.5 cm tall, centred 21 cm forward and 25 cm to the left and to the right of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Contamination, at any moment, scores 0.0 (latched): a gripper (any part of its collision meshes) touching the forceps or the tray; any surface of the pouch (either sheet's faces, folded flaps or pull tabs) touching the tray, its drape or its rim; or the forceps touching anything non-sterile: the table, the holder, a waste bin, the tray's rim, a sheet's outer face, flap or pull tab. In the simulation 'touching' is within 3 mm for points on the grippers' collision meshes (4 mm apart) and within 1.5 mm for the props' surfaces; in a real trial it is any contact seen in the videos. Peeled open: the two sheets pulled at least 12 mm apart at some point. On the drape: the forceps lying inside the tray's rim, their middle less than 1.5 cm above the drape. 1.0: peeled open, the forceps on the drape, each sheet in a waste bin (its middle inside a bin, below its walls' top) and both arms back where they started (each TCP within 5 cm of its start), all without contamination; 0.5: peeled open and the forceps on the drape, without contamination; 0.25: peeled open, without contamination; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the forceps and both sheets still.
reset_notes: Seal a new pouch with the forceps inside and stand it in the holder; empty the bins.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the sheets are stiff 2 mm plates with rigid folded-out flaps; the seal is a prismatic joint against a 600 N/m spring, switched off once the sheets are 12 mm apart; the film is drawn clear. Contact is judged geometrically each step from the props' shapes and points on the grippers' collision meshes, not from the physics engine's contacts. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
